Render a status view for the on-call engineer.

scenarios.title: Payments snapshot
scenarios.prompt: Show me a payments snapshot: revenue today is $12,400, up $1,200 versus yesterday, which is good. Refund rate is 0.8%, flat, nothing remarkable. Failed charges: 23 today and rising, which worries me. Also warn me that the card processor has been reporting degraded performance since 14:10 UTC. I want the numbers to be updatable later without re-sending the components.

scenarios.title: Incident, hard mode
scenarios.prompt: Checkout error rate spiked right after deploy 4190 went out at 14:02 UTC. Show the on-call engineer an incident view: a line chart of the error rate over the last hour (you have five readings at 15-minute intervals: 0.4, 0.5, 2.1, 4.8, 3.9 percent), a table of today's three deploys (payments-api deploy 4190 live at 14:02:11 UTC after 142 seconds, checkout-web canary at 14:10:40 UTC after 98 seconds, search-index failed at 13:55:03 UTC after 311 seconds), and ask them to approve rolling payments-api back to build 4189 — a comment must be required with the decision. Wire everything so the readings and deploy statuses can update live as you learn more.

scenarios.title: Live deploy
scenarios.prompt: You are running a production deploy of payments-api build 4191, currently rolling out: 4 of 10 pods are ready. Show a live deploy view: overall rollout progress; a timeline of what has happened so far (build started at 14:20:05 UTC, canary reported healthy at 14:21:40 UTC which is good, rollout began at 14:22:10 UTC, and at 14:24:02 UTC pod 4's readiness probe started running slow, which is worth watching); the tail of the deploy log (three lines: pulling image, starting pod 4 of 10, waiting on readiness probe for pod 4); and a way to abort the rollout — it's destructive, must have a built-in confirmation step, and when clicked you need to receive the build id and service name. Everything should update live as the rollout progresses.

scenarios.title: Service passport
scenarios.prompt: Render a compact overview of the checkout-web service: its key facts (region eu-west-1, runtime node 24, owned by team payments, last deployed 2026-08-17 at 09:12 UTC), an inline trend of p95 latency over the last twelve readings (178, 182, 175, 190, 260, 240, 210, 195, 188, 199, 205, 214 milliseconds — that spike is concerning), and its current deploy stage, which is Canary. The latency readings should be updatable later without re-sending components.

scenarios.title: Weekly review
scenarios.prompt: Give me the weekly on-call review. Incidents per day this week: Monday 2, Tuesday 0, Wednesday 5, Thursday 1, Friday 3, Saturday 0, Sunday 1 — Wednesday was rough, call that out. Then a sortable table of the four noisiest alerts: HighLatencyP95 fired 41 times, last at 2026-08-15T22:14:00Z; DiskPressure fired 28 times, last at 2026-08-16T03:41:00Z; PodRestartLoop fired 17 times, last at 2026-08-14T11:05:00Z; CertExpirySoon fired 9 times, last at 2026-08-13T09:00:00Z. Finally ask me to approve muting HighLatencyP95 for seven days — no comment needed. Numbers should be updatable later.

scenarios.title: Postmortem intake
scenarios.prompt: Collect an incident postmortem: a severity choice between Sev 1 (total outage), Sev 2 (degraded), and Sev 3 (cosmetic), defaulting to Sev 2; a summary of what happened that must be at least 50 characters; the date the incident started (it can't be in the future — today is 2026-08-19); and whether follow-up review is needed, defaulting to yes. Group the severity and date under a section titled 'Classification' and the rest under 'Details'. On submit you need all four answers.

scenarios.title: Rollback justification
scenarios.prompt: Before you roll payments-api back to build 4189, collect: a justification of at least 30 characters (required), and which environments to roll back — production, staging, or both (at least implied by checkboxes for Production and Staging, defaulting to production only). The submit button should say 'Roll back' and you need the justification and environments when it fires. While you process the rollback the form should show a busy state you can control from your side.

scenarios.title: Service settings
scenarios.prompt: Render a settings form for the checkout-web service: a replica count between 1 and 20 (currently 4), a region select with eu-west-1 (Europe) and us-east-1 (US East), currently eu-west-1, and a toggle for canary deploys, currently off. scenarios.title: Developer survey
scenarios.prompt: A two-part developer survey. Part 'About you': role (select: Engineer, SRE, Manager), years of experience (number, 0 to 50). Part 'Your tooling': which CI systems they use from GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CircleCI (any number), and one thing they'd change about their deploy process (free text, optional, up to 500 characters). Submit says 'Send survey'. You need every answer on submit.

scenarios.title: Sign-up with checks
scenarios.prompt: A sign-up form: email (required, valid email), a handle that must be 3-15 characters of lowercase letters, digits or dashes only (required — explain the format to the user when it fails), and a start date no earlier than 2026-09-01. On submit, named 'Create account', you need the email and handle, and you'll confirm account creation asynchronously from your side.
